name: SAML Tokens
description: An adversary may forge SAML tokens with any permissions claims and lifetimes if they possess a valid SAML token-signing certificate.(Citation: Microsoft SolarWinds Steps) The default lifetime of a SAML token is one hour, but the validity period can be specified in the NotOnOrAfter value of the conditions ... element in a token. This value can be changed using the AccessTokenLifetime in a LifetimeTokenPolicy.(Citation: Microsoft SAML Token Lifetimes) Forged SAML tokens enable adversaries to authenticate across services that use SAML 2.0 as an SSO (single sign-on) mechanism.(Citation: Cyberark Golden SAML) An adversary may utilize [Private Keys](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/004) to compromise an organization's token-signing certificate to create forged SAML tokens. If the adversary has sufficient permissions to establish a new federation trust with their own Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS) server, they may instead generate their own trusted token-signing certificate.(Citation: Microsoft SolarWinds Customer Guidance) This differs from [Steal Application Access Token](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1528) and other similar behaviors in that the tokens are new and forged by the adversary, rather than stolen or intercepted from legitimate users. An adversary may gain administrative Entra ID privileges if a SAML token is forged which claims to represent a highly privileged account. This may lead to [Use Alternate Authentication Material](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1550), which may bypass multi-factor and other authentication protection mechanisms.(Citation: Microsoft SolarWinds Customer Guidance)

telemetry.name: Logon Session Creation
telemetry.description: Creation of a logon session with account and logon-type context.
telemetry.collection_focus: Enable Audit Logon and collect successful session creation on the receiving host; join session/logon IDs rather than only account names.

providers.name: Windows Security auditing
providers.scope: Policy-dependent account, object, task and logon records on the host that performs the operation.

configuration: Use a lab-only GPO under Computer Configuration → Windows Settings → Security Settings → Advanced Audit Policy Configuration. Enable the specific subcategory named below.
For object-level auditing, configure a narrow system access control list (SACL) on the test object in addition to policy. Do not audit an entire production directory by default.

Forward Security events from the responsible host or controller; retain subject and target identities, object identifiers, result and original XML. Confirm effective policy with auditpol /get /category:*.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: A policy checkbox alone does not guarantee an event. Host role, SACL, success/failure selection and audit policy precedence matter. Directory changes may arrive as multiple records.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per principal, host and object: unusual access/request rates, new principal-object relationships, and changes outside approved administration windows. Control for service accounts and scheduled directory maintenance.

telemetry.name: Logon Session Metadata
telemetry.description: Attributes of existing logon sessions and their association with accounts or hosts.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect supported session inventory and correlate session IDs with authentication, logon and logoff events.

providers.name: osquery
providers.scope: Scheduled host-state queries; supported tables and privileges vary by OS. Select a table that actually exposes the required object.

providers.name: Linux Audit plus inventory snapshots
providers.scope: Events explain changes; snapshots describe state at collection time.

configuration: Define the inventory query, allowed host set, interval and least-privileged reader. Store a stable asset ID, observation time and collector version.
Keep successive snapshots and calculate additions, removals and changed attributes. Pair state changes with audit events when available.
Export collector health and missed-poll counts so a missing snapshot is not misclassified as a missing asset.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Snapshots miss short-lived objects and do not identify who caused a change. A generic inventory agent is not guaranteed to expose firmware or kernel-level details.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Compare authorized state snapshots: first-seen drivers/services/modules, unexpected configuration drift and integrity changes. Record collection cadence; absence in a sample is not evidence of deletion.

telemetry.name: User Account Authentication
telemetry.description: Authentication attempts and outcomes for a user or workload account.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect successful and failed sign-ins, authentication method, application and conditional-access context; distinguish account validation from session creation.

strategies.name: Detection Strategy for Forged SAML Tokens

analytics.name: Analytic 0418
analytics.guidance: Forged SAML tokens can be observed as authentication attempts with valid signatures but missing expected preceding Kerberos or authentication events. Defenders may correlate SAML assertions with absent Event IDs 4769, 1200, or 1202, or tokens issued with abnormal lifetimes, issuers, or claims compared to baseline.

tuning.description: Defines the maximum expected lifetime of a SAML token (e.g., >1 hour considered anomalous).
List of approved SAML issuers and certificate thumbprints.

log_sources.name: azure:signinlogs
log_sources.channel: SAML-based login with anomalous issuer or NotOnOrAfter lifetime

analytics.name: Analytic 0419
analytics.guidance: Forged SAML tokens in IaaS environments often manifest as cross-cloud or cross-account authentication without matching STS events. Defenders may see AssumeRole or GetFederationToken API usage without a corresponding SAML assertion log from the trusted IdP.

tuning.description: Flag SAML tokens used across unexpected accounts or cloud tenants.

log_sources.name: CloudTrail:Signin
log_sources.channel: SAML login without corresponding IdP authentication log

analytics.name: Analytic 0420
analytics.guidance: Forged SAML tokens may be used on Windows systems to authenticate to federated apps without normal Kerberos activity. Defenders may detect anomalous event correlation, where access to SaaS/O365 via SAML occurs without prior TGT requests or user logons.

tuning.description: Number of unusual claims in a SAML token (e.g., excessive privileges).

log_sources.name: WinEventLog:ADFS
log_sources.channel: Token issuance events showing anomalous claims or issuers

analytics.name: Analytic 0421
analytics.guidance: Forged SAML tokens can appear as SaaS logins where authentication succeeded without MFA, or where tokens contain claims inconsistent with the user profile. Look for concurrent sessions across different geographies with the same SAML assertion ID.

tuning.description: Triggers when same SAML token used in different geographies within short timeframe.

log_sources.name: saas:access
log_sources.channel: SAML token accepted without preceding login challenge

log_sources.name: m365:unified
log_sources.channel: Abnormal user claims or unexpected elevated role assignment in SAML assertion

analytics.name: Analytic 0422
analytics.guidance: Forged SAML tokens may be leveraged to access O365 apps such as Outlook or SharePoint. Defenders should monitor for token replay across multiple clients or access attempts to privileged mailboxes without prior interactive login.

tuning.description: Number of times a token is reused within short timeframe.

log_sources.name: m365:exchange
log_sources.channel: Mailbox access using SAML token without corresponding MFA event

log_sources.name: m365:sharepoint
log_sources.channel: File access with forged or anomalous SAML claims

software.name: AADInternals
software.description: [AADInternals](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0677) can be used to create SAML tokens using the AD Federated Services token signing certificate.(Citation: AADInternals Documentation)

references.description: Dr. Nestori Syynimaa. (2018, October 25). AADInternals. Retrieved February 18, 2022.

mitigations.name: Active Directory Configuration
mitigations.description: For containing the impact of a previously forged SAML token, rotate the token-signing AD FS certificate in rapid succession twice, which will invalidate any tokens generated using the previous certificate.(Citation: Mandiant Defend UNC2452 White Paper)

references.description: Mandiant. (2021, January 19). Remediation and Hardening Strategies for Microsoft 365 to Defend Against UNC2452. Retrieved January 22, 2021.

mitigations.name: User Account Management
mitigations.description: Ensure that user accounts with administrative rights follow best practices, including use of privileged access workstations, Just in Time/Just Enough Administration (JIT/JEA), and strong authentication. Reduce the number of users that are members of highly privileged Directory Roles.(Citation: Microsoft SolarWinds Customer Guidance)

references.description: MSRC. (2020, December 13). Customer Guidance on Recent Nation-State Cyber Attacks. Retrieved December 17, 2020.

mitigations.name: Privileged Account Management
mitigations.description: Restrict permissions and access to the AD FS server to only originate from privileged access workstations.(Citation: FireEye ADFS)

references.description: Bierstock, D., Baker, A. (2019, March 21). I am AD FS and So Can You. Retrieved December 17, 2020.

mitigations.name: Audit
mitigations.description: Enable advanced auditing on AD FS. Check the success and failure audit options in the AD FS Management snap-in. Enable Audit Application Generated events on the AD FS farm via Group Policy Object.(Citation: FireEye ADFS)

references.description: Bierstock, D., Baker, A. (2019, March 21). I am AD FS and So Can You. Retrieved December 17, 2020.

candidates.name: Golden SAML
candidates.description:
Forge a "Golden SAML" token which allows to impersonate any Azure AD user, and authenticate to AADGraph (as a proof). 
You will need the ADFS token signing certificate (see T1552.004 to export it).
More info here : https://o365blog.com/post/adfs/

certificate_path.description: Token signing certificate path. See T1552.004 to export it

immutable_id.description: ImmutableId of the targeted user. It can be obtained with AzureAD powershell module; $(Get-AzureADUser -SearchString "username").ImmutableId

issuer_uri.description: Issuer URI of the ADFS service

simulation.prerequisites: Use disposable lab hosts and test accounts, explicit target allowlists, a clean snapshot, bounded egress and a restore plan. Review every candidate and dependency before any execution.

synthetic.purpose: Collection/parser contract exercise, NOT a positive example or detection of this TTP.
